verses.1: This is what the LORD says: Go down to the house of the king of Judah and speak there this message:
verses.2: Say: Listen to the word of the LORD, King of Judah, you who sit on the throne of David, you and your servants and the people entering through these gates.
verses.3: This is what the LORD says: Do justice and righteousness, rescue the one being robbed from the hand of the oppressor. Do not mistreat the foreigner, the orphan, or the widow. Do not spill innocent blood in this place.
verses.4: If you do this, then the kings who sit on David’s throne will come through these gates, riding in chariots and on horses—both he and his servants and his people.
verses.5: But if you do not listen to these words, I swear by myself, says the LORD, that this house will become a ruin.
verses.6: For the LORD says concerning the house of the king of Judah: You are like Gilead to me, the head of Lebanon. If not, I will make you a wasteland, a city not inhabited.
verses.7: I will bring destroyers against you, man and sword, who will cut down your choice cedars and cast them into the fire.
verses.8: Many nations will pass by this city and ask each other, “Why has the LORD done this to this great city?”
verses.9: They will say, “Because they broke the covenant of the LORD their God and worshipped other gods and served them.”
verses.10: Do not mourn for the dead or cry for him. Wail for the one who is going into exile, for he will not return. He will never see the land of his birth again.
verses.11: For this is what the LORD says about Shallum son of Jehoiakim, the king who rules in place of Jehoiakim his father, who left this place: He will not return there again.
verses.12: In the place where I have exiled him, he will die. He will never see this land again.
verses.13: Woe to the one who builds his house with injustice and his upper rooms with dishonesty, who makes his workers toil for nothing and does not pay them their wages.
verses.14: He says, “I will build myself a magnificent house with spacious upper rooms, with large windows and cedar floors, and I will anoint it with costly oil.”
verses.15: Are you a king because you surround yourself with cedar? Your father ate and drank and did justice and righteousness. That is why it was good for him.
verses.16: He ruled in favor of the oppressed and the poor. That is what it means to know me, says the LORD.
verses.17: But your eyes and your heart are greedy only for your own gain and for shedding innocent blood. You oppress and murder.
verses.18: Therefore this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim son of Jehoiakim, the king of Judah: They will not mourn for him: “Woe, brother! Woe, sister!” They will not mourn for him: “Woe, master! Woe, honored one!”
verses.19: Like a burial for a donkey, he will be buried, dragged away and thrown beyond the gates of Jerusalem.
verses.20: Go up to Lebanon and cry out. Raise your voice in Bashan. Call out from across the sea, for all your lovers have been shattered.
verses.21: I spoke to you in your rebellion, but you said, “I will not listen.” This has been your way from your youth, for you have not obeyed my voice.
verses.22: All your shepherds will be scattered by the wind, and your lovers will go into captivity. Then you will be put to shame and disgraced by all your friends.
verses.23: You who dwell in Lebanon, who take pride in your cedars, you will wail as a woman in childbirth when pain comes upon you.
verses.24: I swear by myself, says the LORD, that if Jehucam son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, is a signet ring on my right hand, I will still tear you away from me.
verses.25: I will hand you over to those who seek your life, to those you fear, and to the Babylonian king and to the Chaldeans.
verses.26: I will cast you and your mother who bore you into another land, one where you were not born. There you will die.
verses.27: And to the land they long for to return to, they will never return.
verses.28: This man, Jeconiah, is like a broken jar, an object of no value. Why were he and his descendants cast out and thrown into a land they did not know?
verses.29: Earth, earth, hear the word of the LORD!
verses.30: This is what the LORD says: Write this man down as childless, a man who will not succeed in his days, for none of his descendants will sit on the throne of David or rule again in Judah.

notes:
Notes
- v. 24: The name "Jeconiah" (יְהוֹכִין) is used here instead of "Jehucam" (יְהוּכַם), a variant reading; "Jeconiah" is the standard form, but "Jehucam" aligns with the Masoretic consonantal text. Both spellings are acceptable.
- v. 30: "Write this man down as childless" reflects the meaning of עֲרִירִי, an unusual term often translated as "a desolate one," but here used to emphasize the divine decree that Jeconiah’s line will not produce a ruler.
